the Blessed One {the Teacher} addressed the monks: 'Monks!'
'Hey, Kālī!' 'What, madam?' 'Why did you get up after daybreak?'
'Is form constant or inconstant?' 'Inconstant, lord.' 'And is that which is inconstant stressful or pleasant?' 'Stressful, lord.'
'Do you understand, monk?' 'Yes, lord, I understand.'
'Where is Mahā Moggallāna… Where is Mahā Kassapa… Where is Mahā Kaccāna?'
'This is peace… this is exquisite… the pacification of all fabrications…'
'This is stress… this is the origination of stress… this is the cessation of stress…'
'Well, yes.' 'Oh, indeed.' 'See, look.' 'Look, see.'
'Listen, monk.' 'Speak, friend.' 'Right, then.'
'Yes, lord, it is.' 'No, friend, indeed.' 'So, let it be.'
'Come, friend, see.' 'Go, monk, now.' 'Thus, it is.'
'Always mindful… always alert… heedful, they prosper.'
'Mindful, they wake… stilled, they dwell… released, they rejoice.'
'Calmed, they sit… tranquil, they stay… peaceful, they live.'
'Unbound, they wake… ceased, all is quiet.'
'Look, the moon… look, the stars… listen, the wind…'
'Listen, the sound… speak, wise one… listen, disciple…'
'This, indeed, is peace… that, indeed, is Unbinding…'
'Indeed, it is stilled… indeed, it has ceased…'
'Always quiet… always stilled… silently, they sit…'
'Gently, they speak… wise, they are… noble, they live…'
